rulings.challenge_claim: The row's assertion that "10:31 and 10:32 both end on" תהפכות is byte-false for 10:31: its actual final word is תכרת, with תהפכות as the construct-chain noun before it.
rulings.grounds: Word-split of oshb bytes for 10:31 (7 words) gives final word תִּכָּרֵֽת ("will be cut off"), with תַּ֝הְפֻּכ֗וֹת sitting at word 6 of 7, construct-medial before that closing verb. 10:32 (7 words) genuinely ends on תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת (word 7 of 7). Re-ran the skeleton sweep of תהפכות: 9 verses book-wide (Prov.2.12, 2.14, 6.14, 8.13, 10.31, 10.32, 16.28, 16.30, 23.33), with 10:31-10:32 the sweep's only adjacent pair, and the verse-initial opener parallel פי צדיק / שפתי צדיק confirmed at word-initial position -- so the cluster's headline cohesion argument survives untouched; only the 'both end on' phrasing overstates the parallel for 10:31. Distinct from this row's other (LF) item: that one is a citation-completeness gap, this one is a word-position accuracy error in the rationale itself -- two different defect objects on the same row, not a duplicate.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the rationale/observed_substrate_signals sentence to state that תהפכות is 10:32's final word and 10:31's construct-medial noun (word 6 of 7), not 10:31's own closing word. Cure test: a word-index byte check (collate.py byte tier + explicit split) against both verses' final tokens must pass -- the same check that surfaces this defect.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's claim that 11:5 and 11:6 share a verb construction with a third-person-plural (3mp) object suffix, run consecutively across both verses, is byte-false for 11:5, which is grammatically singular throughout.
rulings.grounds: Word-level check of oshb bytes: 11:5's guidance verb תְּיַשֵּׁ֣ר carries NO pronominal suffix at all; its object is the separate noun דַּרְכּ֑וֹ ("his way"), which carries a 3ms suffix agreeing with the singular referent ("the blameless one"); the parallel verb יִפֹּ֥ל ("he falls") is likewise 3ms. Only 11:6 is genuinely plural: תַּצִּילֵ֑ם ("delivers THEM") carries a real 3mp object suffix, and יִלָּכֵֽדוּ ("they are trapped") is 3mp, both agreeing with the plural referents. LF and OL independently converge on this SAME defect (LF via the דרכו/יפל forms, OL via the more precise point that תישר itself takes no suffix at all) -- merged into one ruling, source 'both'. The headline cluster evidence is untouched: re-ran the skeleton sweep of צדקת and reconfirmed exactly 2 verses book-wide, both this adjacent pair -- the exclusive construct-opener grounds stand on their own without the suffix claim.
rulings.remedy: Replace the 'shared...3mp-suffix...run consecutively' clause in rationale and observed_substrate_signals with an accurate description: 11:5 is singular (bare verb + 3ms-suffixed object, 3ms parallel verb); 11:6 is plural (3mp-suffixed verb, 3mp parallel verb). The shared ground is the exclusive construct-opener (צדקת, 2 verses book-wide) plus a vice-triggered-downfall template, not person/number uniformity. Cure test: a targeted morphological byte-check of the four cited verb/suffix forms must pass before the row ships.

rulings.challenge_claim: 11:8 and 11:9 share the book's sole occurrence of the root חלץ (Niphal, "delivered"), applied to the righteous in both verses; the row's rejected_alternative wrongly states 11:9 'finds nothing to match' 11:8.
rulings.grounds: RE-DERIVED independently per the adjudication note, not trusted from the packets. Object swept: root occurrences of חלץ, allography-aware (final-tsade and medial-tsade spellings, since the root's only allographic letter is its final צ/ץ). sweep.py --skel חלץ (final-tsade, word-final position) = exactly 1 hit, Prov.11.8 (נֶחֱלָ֑ץ). sweep.py --skel חלצ (medial-tsade, required because 11:9's form is not word-final) = exactly 1 hit, Prov.11.9 (יֵחָלֵֽצוּ). Combined allography-aware total: the root occurs in exactly 2 verses book-wide, both halves of this row's own seam, both Niphal, both predicated of the righteous (צדיק/צדיקים). This matches and upholds LF's and OL's claim exactly. P05-041's own rejected_alternative (quoted verbatim from draft_rows_combined.jsonl): "No pairing is drawn with 11:9: this verse's trouble/substitution pair finds nothing to match it in that verse's mouth/knowledge contrast" -- byte-false given the shared-root finding. This exclusivity (1+1=2 total) is rarer than the sweep grounds this same writer wave treated as decisive for the 10:31-10:32 (תהפכות=9 verses) and 11:5-11:6 (צדקת=2 verses) cluster calls in this same part, yet it is undisclosed and actively denied here. LF and OL raise the SAME defect (same object, same 1+1 sweep) -- merged, source 'both'.
rulings.remedy: SEAM-PAIR CURE (Job lesson a): author the fix once, install identically on P05-041 and P05-042. For P05-041: rewrite rejected_alternative to disclose and correctly characterize the חלץ link rather than deny it -- e.g., state that 11:9 shares the book's only other occurrence of the root (Niphal, applied to the righteous) with this verse, while still arguing image divergence (substitution vs. mouth/knowledge) if the row maintains separate rows. Cure test: observed_substrate_signals must carry the digit-bearing, allography-aware root-sweep citation (1+1=2) per the book's universal-claim-needs-a-sweep-digit discipline -- the same check that exposed this gap. GRANULARITY FLAG (boss-adoption proposal only, NOT a peer ruling): whether this root-exclusivity meets the §6 cluster bar (re-classifying 11:8-11:9 as proverb_cluster) is a genuinely closer call than the accepted 10:31-32/11:5-6 clusters, since 11:8 and 11:9's own images remain distinct (substitution vs. mouth/knowledge) unlike those pairs' shared construction runs. Flagged for the boss round; not decided here.
